title: Authentication trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for authentication-flow trace events.

credentialStyle.description: Where the truth lives: a server-side session record, or a signed token held by the client.

passwordStorage.description: How the user store keeps secrets at rest.

clock.description: Model time in minutes since the run started.

accessLifetime.description: How long an issued credential stays valid, in minutes.

loginRateLimit.description: Wrong passwords tolerated per account; 0 when logins are not throttled.

users.description: The user store — what the server keeps at rest.

stored.description: The stored value: a hash, or (in the anti-pattern) the password itself.

salt.description: Per-user salt; empty when passwords are stored in plaintext.

secondFactor.description: Whether this account also requires a second factor.

failedAttempts.description: Consecutive wrong passwords, reset by a successful login.

serverStore.description: Credentials the server remembers. Always empty in token mode — that is the point.

action.description: What the current step is doing.

kind.description: Which part of the lifecycle is running.

actor.description: Who is acting; may differ from the credential's user when one is replayed.

detail.description: The username, path or amount of time this step is about.

phases.description: The five phases every authentication walks, in order, with the verdict of each for the current step.

status.description: pending = never reached; breach = it let through what it should have stopped.

detail.description: Bare token behind the verdict: a username, a credential id or a reason.

identity.description: Who the server decided the caller is; null while nobody has been identified.

source.description: What the identity was read from.

status.description: HTTP status the server answered with; null while the step is still running.

decision.description: breach = the request was served and should not have been.

reason.description: Technical code for the refusal or the breach; null when nothing went wrong.

detail.description: The offending user, credential id, code or expiry; empty when not applicable.

stats.description: Running totals across the whole run.

served.description: Requests the server answered as a known caller.

refused.description: Requests refused because nobody could be identified.

breaches.description: Requests served that should not have been.

id.description: The value the client sends back: a session id or a token.

kind.description: Which credential style this one is.

state.description: pending = the second factor is not done; dropped = the client let go of it.
